concerns.text: Task T004 declares a dependency on T005b, but T005b (Write Data Model) is listed *after* T004. This violates the producer‑before‑consumer rule; the data model must exist before utils can be implemented.
Because T004 also depends on T005b, the listed order makes T004 unexecutable until a later task runs, breaking the deterministic FR‑010 ordering.

Task T040b (Create Quickstart Documentation) is marked [P] with no explicit dependency on T001 (Create project structure). If T040b runs before T001, the quickstart file may reference directories that do not yet exist, creating an ordering conflict.

concerns.location: User Story 2 – Phase 3 – T025, T026, T027
concerns.text: All US‑2 tasks depend on T019 (US‑1 data generation). This creates a cross‑story dependency, contradicting the requirement that each user story be independently implementable and testable.

US‑3 tasks depend on training logs produced by US‑2 (e.g., T025, T027). This again violates the independent‑story principle; US‑3 should be able to run on its own artifact set without requiring US‑2 to be completed first.

T025/T027 write JSON files to `data/logs/…` while the plan (Project Structure) defines `data/processed/trajectories/` and `data/processed/convergence_logs.csv`. The mismatch creates a path‑dependency conflict with the agreed data model.
T022 saves graphs to `data/raw/graphs.jsonl` but does not include a step to generate and record a checksum as required by Constitution Principle III. This omission breaks the data‑hygiene pipeline.

Tasks draft entities into `code/data_model_draft.md`, yet the Constitution (Principle III) forbids in‑place drafts and requires the final `data-model.md` to be the authoritative artifact. Using a draft file violates the data‑hygiene and single‑source‑of‑truth rules.
